title: Looker API Usage and Rate Limiting
dataSources: Looker System Activity (`history`, `pdt_builds`, `scheduled_plan`, `event`, `api_usage`), Looker API queue/PDT metrics, GCP audit logs for Looker Studio and BigQuery-backed reports.
app: Looker System Activity and Admin API via HEC scripted inputs; Looker Studio and BigQuery-backed usage via the Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform (`Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`).
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=looker:system_activity view=api_usage
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as calls, sum(eval(http_status=429)) as throttled by api_client, _time
| where throttled>0
| sort - _time
description: Tracks Looker API call volume by client and flags rate-limited (HTTP 429) calls, which break embeds and integrations relying on the API.
value: API rate-limiting silently breaks embedded analytics and automations; per-client visibility shows which integration to throttle or upgrade.
implementation: Query the `api_usage` view or ingest API access logs; schedule hourly; alert on sustained 429s per client.
visualization: Timechart of API calls vs throttled, table by client.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the automated connections into Looker and flag when they get blocked for asking too often, so embedded reports keep working.
